text:
incident-bot: Pager P0 — streaming tail latency spike (eu-west-1)

incident-bot: Multiple customer reports + elevated 5xx and streaming stalls on chat.generate since 11:02 UTC. Error rate ~3.2% on streaming path. Paging oncall.

Priya Kaur: on it. taking lead. currently gathering quick metrics. any immediate mitigations we can try?

Ethan Wu: seeing a spike in async queue depth on the streaming workers. something is causing long GC/eviction on the KV cache processes. logs show repeated `retry=3` errors from rpc->runtime.

Priya Kaur: quick plan: 1) throttle long seq jobs to secondary pool, 2) scale up worker pool in eu-west by +30% (temp), 3) craft status page initial message. Liam can you draft initial copy? I'll confirm customer impact numbers.

Liam O'Connor: copying a quick draft for the status page and customer notice. please review:

```
Initial update (11:10 UTC): We are investigating an issue causing higher-than-normal latency and occasional failed streaming responses for chat generation in the eu-west region. Customers using streaming chat endpoints may see delayed tokens or intermittent errors. We are actively routing traffic and applying mitigations. We will post updates every 15 minutes. No data exposure is suspected at this time.
```

Liam O'Connor: quick internal note: state we estimate ~3-6% of streaming requests affected; Dedicated EU customers: two clusters hit heavy (IDs: dc-eu-12, dc-eu-23) — we should offer Ops team ping if they want failover guidance.

Sara Kim: +1 to that copy. Add an "affected customers" line? e.g., 'Some Dedicated customers may see higher error rates; hosted API customers may experience increased tail latency.'

Priya Kaur: please don't call out internal cluster IDs in public message. Liam remove IDs from public copy. keep them in internal thread.

Liam O'Connor: updated public copy:

```
Initial update (11:12 UTC): We are investigating an issue causing higher-than-normal latency and occasional failed streaming responses for chat generation in the eu-west region. Some customers using streaming endpoints may experience delayed tokens or intermittent errors. We are actively routing traffic and applying mitigations. No data exposure is suspected at this time. We will post updates every 15 minutes.
```

Grace Chen: legal ok to publish; no PII at risk per quick check. @Customer Ops please prepare a short email for customers on paid support.

Customer Ops: will draft an outbound note once we have the first mitigation result. ETA 11:25 UTC.

Ethan Wu: mitigation in progress: scaling worker pool + throttling long-seqs. I'll also roll back the KV cache GC tweak that landed in last deploy — doing that now.

Priya Kaur: please post the initial status update to status page and ping on support channels once published. Liam, post the public text as is. I'll add internal context below.

Liam O'Connor: published initial update at 11:15 UTC. link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/streaming-latency-eu-2026

Priya Kaur: internal context snippet (do not publish):
- rollback of KV cache GC tweak triggered less frequent but longer GC pauses; those pauses were causing backlog and RPC timeouts. Root repro in staging pending.
- affected path: streaming token emission code path -> stall when KV eviction occurs

Ethan Wu: mitigation shows early signal: error rate down from 3.2% -> 0.9% after rollback and scale-up (11:23 UTC). still watching.

Liam O'Connor: drafting update #2 for status page draft:

```
Update (11:25 UTC): We have applied mitigations that have reduced the error rate and improved streaming performance. Error rate is currently reduced and we continue to monitor. We will provide another update within 30 minutes or sooner if the situation changes.
```

Sara Kim: looks good. add 'affected endpoints: chat streaming' line for clarity.

Liam O'Connor: updated and posted at 11:27 UTC.

Priya Kaur: heads-up to customer success: escalate any high-severity customer reports; offer manual failover assistance for Dedicated customers.

Customer Ops: we've queued targeted outreach for 4 impacted accounts; sending now.

Grace Chen: any regulatory customers we need to notify specially? recall EU customers have stricter SLAs.

Priya Kaur: flagged two EU enterprise accounts privately. Ops team handling via private channel.

Ethan Wu: monitoring: tail latency improved for short sequences; heavy long-seq jobs still have occasional stalls. next step is to throttle long-seq job admission for 30 minutes to fully drain backlog.

Priya Kaur: do the throttle and post an update once in effect.

Ethan Wu: throttle applied at 11:45 UTC. immediate telemetry: queue depth down 45% and error rate 0.3% (11:52 UTC).

Liam O'Connor: ready to publish final resolve draft once QA confirms stable for 30 mins. Suggested resolved copy below:

```
Resolved (12:18 UTC): The issue causing elevated streaming latency and intermittent failed responses in eu-west has been resolved. The root cause was a regression in KV cache GC behavior introduced in a recent change; we rolled that back and scaled worker capacity to clear the backlog. Error rates have returned to normal and streaming performance is stable. We are scheduling a full post-incident review and will share findings and follow-ups within the next week. If you continue to experience issues, please contact support.
```

Priya Kaur: confirmed stable 30m window ended at 12:18 UTC. Good to publish resolve. Also create internal postmortem ticket.

Liam O'Connor: published resolved notice at 12:20 UTC and pinged customers and status subscribers.

Grace Chen: adding note to postmortem: check release gating for KV cache changes and add canary for streaming path.

Priya Kaur: thanks team. postmortem lead: @Ethan Wu. oncall handoff: none needed, incident resolved. closing thread.

incident-bot: Incident closed by Priya Kaur at 12:22 UTC. Incident ID INC-2026-045
